clue.text: Leaving artillery, becoming very successful

great guns are heavy artillery pieces

explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to be going great guns is to be doing extremely well and making rapid progress.

clue.text: Fashionable former partner's put on sham woolly

parts.note: in means fashionable

an act is a pretence or sham

explanation.surface: An ex who is fashionable puts on a fake woolly garment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'woolly' looks like a jumper; it means vague.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: vague and imprecise, not sharply defined.

clue.text: Man put fish on fork

parts.note: a gar is a long-snouted fish
Y is shaped like a fork in the road

explanation.surface: A man spears a fish on his fork.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a man's first name.

clue.text: Light in arcade flickering

indicators.note: flickering suggests unsteady movement, so the letters of in arcade are shifted around

explanation.surface: Light flickering in an amusement arcade.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: brightness or glow given off by something shining.

clue.text: From bygone days, energy has to go into a medal

parts.note: a gold is a first-place medal

clue.text: Acquire schoolboy grub seized by error — eat up!

clue.text: Itinerant lunatic standing in certainly not in charge

mad means lunatic

clue.text: Help cynic to set off for college

clue.text: Resent having to ask for charity, urged otherwise

parts.note: to beg is to ask for alms

explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to begrudge something is to feel bitter or envious about it.

clue.text: Scoring rate?

parts.note: suggests runs or goals per game, but scoring is writing music, and a piece's rate is its speed

explanation.surface: A sports question about how fast points are piling up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scoring' looks like sport; in music a score is written, and the speed it is played at is its rate.
explanation.definitionFit: Musical term: the speed at which a written piece is meant to be performed.

clue.text: Certain Irish football official joining United board

parts.note: a ref is a football referee
U is the abbreviation for United in team names
a table is a board for meals

explanation.surface: An Irish referee joins the board of a club called United.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: impossible to disprove, beyond doubt.

clue.text: By river, paddle and shout

parts.note: R is the map abbreviation for river
an oar is a paddle for rowing

explanation.surface: Someone rowing by a river, splashing and yelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a loud bellow or cry.

clue.text: Stop working for, say, 24 hours?

definitions.meaning: to finish work for the time being
taken literally, to name a 24-hour period, that is, to give it its everyday label

explanation.surface: Knocking off work, perhaps for a whole day.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes the idiom literally: naming a 24-hour span.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: deciding to stop an activity, especially work, for now; read literally, labelling a period of time.

clue.text: Legendary Irish character ruined her clean-up

clue.text: Channel follows bridge players making fix

a trench is a channel dug in the ground

explanation.surface: A channel trailing card players while they make something firm.
explanation.walkthrough: Bridge players are named by compass points: N, E, S, W.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to establish something firmly so it is hard to dislodge.

clue.text: What can be made from dripping in the freezer

definitions.text: What can be made from dripping in the freezer

parts.words: What can be made from dripping in the freezer
parts.note: dripping sounds like cooking fat stored cold, but it is water dripping in freezing weather

explanation.surface: A kitchen tip about what to do with saved fat kept in the freezer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dripping' suggests beef fat; really it is water dripping in freezing cold.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a hanging spike of ice formed when dripping water freezes.

clue.text: Church welcomes Irishman, one that's put up memorial

indicators.note: the church takes the other letters inside it

taken as written

clue.text: King hiding in a French shack, safe and sound

clue.text: Bravely willing to hold a function

parts.note: to have is to hold
to go is to work or function

explanation.surface: Someone bold enough to host a party.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a have-a-go hero is a member of the public who tackles a criminal.
explanation.definitionFit: British adjective for a member of the public prepared to confront wrongdoers courageously.

clue.text: He's livid, agitated yet mischievous

indicators.note: agitated means stirred up, so the letters of he's livid are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A man furious and worked up, yet playfully naughty.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: wickedly playful, like an imp.

clue.text: Fashion is okay with university — heaven help us!

indicators.note: to fashion is to shape, so the letters of is okay are moulded anew

explanation.surface: An exasperated cry that fashion at a university is apparently fine.

clue.text: Rubbish, getting snared by evil drug

indicators.note: the rubbish is trapped inside the evil word

tat is cheap rubbish

explanation.surface: Trash caught in a wicked drug trade.

clue.text: Commercial role being a defender

parts.note: a commercial is an advertisement, an ad
a vocation is one's calling or role in life

explanation.surface: A job in advertising compared with life as a defender.

clue.text: Feasting consuming wine

indicators.note: the word feasting swallows up the answer within its letters

clue.text: Animal from a shopping centre taken back

parts.note: a mall is a shopping centre

explanation.surface: An animal being returned from a shopping centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a South American camelid kept for wool and as a pack beast.

clue.text: Vehicle tracks in market from east and west, say, after crashing

indicators.note: in an across answer, read from the east means right to left

parts.note: a mart is a market
W is the compass abbreviation for west

indicators.note: crashing suggests the word say is smashed into a jumble

explanation.surface: Something crashing in a market, with vehicles coming from both directions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from east' reverses the market word, as an across answer is read west to east; 'after crashing' jumbles 'say', which sits after the west letter.

clue.text: Blue feathers being chewed

parts.note: down is soft fine feathers
food being chewed is in the mouth
